what: 1. get_distributionLUT(): a different distribution per trait
title: Getting-LUTs
text: Real leaf/canopy traits don’t follow distribution shape. Chlorophyll content (Cab) tends cluster around typical value (Gaussian-like); leaf-angle parameter LIDFa tendency across mixed canopy (closer Uniform). get_distributionLUT() lets trait pick shape instead forcing one distribution . Define sampling range (minval/maxval, one column per trait) , separately, distribution trait uses: Traits marked "Gaussian" need mean standard deviation (traits left Mean_gauss/Std_gauss – everything "Uniform" – simply ignored part):
code: minval <- data.frame('N' = 1.5, 'Cab' = 5, 'Car' = 0, 'Anth' = 0, 'Cbrown' = 0.0,                       'EWT' = 0.001, 'Prot' = 0.00001, 'CBC' = 0.00001,                       'LIDFa' = 0, 'LAI' = 0.5,                       ### input for INFORM                       LAIu = 0, sd = 200, cd = 0.2, h = 5,                       ### input for fourSAIL-2                       fraction_brown = 0, diss = 0.1, Cv = 0.3, Zeta = 0)  maxval <- data.frame('N' = 3, 'Cab' = 70, 'Car' = 25, 'Anth' = 7, 'Cbrown' = 0.2,                       'EWT' = 0.035, 'Prot' = 0.03, 'CBC' = 0.03,                       'LIDFa' = 70, 'LAI' = 7,                       ### input for INFORM                       LAIu = 0.8, sd = 1000, cd = 7, h = 20,                       ### input for fourSAIL-2                       fraction_brown = 1, diss = 1, Cv = 1, Zeta = 0.2)  TypeDistrib <- data.frame('N' = 'Gaussian', 'Cab' = 'Gaussian', 'Car' = 'Gaussian',                            'Anth' = 'Uniform', 'Cbrown' = 'Uniform',                            'EWT' = 'Uniform', 'Prot' = 'Uniform', 'CBC' = 'Uniform',                            'LIDFa' = 'Uniform', 'LAI' = 'Gaussian',                            ### input for INFORM                            LAIu = 'Uniform', sd = 'Uniform', cd = 'Uniform', h = 'Uniform',                            ### input for fourSAIL-2                            fraction_brown = 'Uniform', diss = 'Uniform', Cv = 'Uniform', Zeta = 'Uniform') Mean_gauss <- data.frame('N' = 2.2, 'Cab' = 45, 'Car' = 8, 'LAI' = 2.25) std_gauss <- Mean_gauss / 2.0 nSamples <- 500 data.LUT <- get_distributionLUT(minval = minval, maxval = maxval,                                  nSamples = nSamples, TypeDistrib = TypeDistrib,                                  Mean_gauss = Mean_gauss, Std_gauss = std_gauss,                                  DepCab = FALSE, setseed = 246)

what: 2. A train/test split, shared by every method
title: Trait inversion: merit-function matching, ML, and deep learning
text: 70/30 split feeds get.inversionOpt() (reference LUT vs. “observed” test spectra), get.inversion() (training data vs. prediction targets), getMLmodel() – comparison end apples--apples.
code: set.seed(1) train_idx <- sample(seq_len(n_samples), size = round(0.7 * n_samples)) test_idx  <- setdiff(seq_len(n_samples), train_idx)  LUT_train <- LUT[train_idx, ] LUT_test  <- LUT[test_idx, ] se2a_mat  <- as.matrix(se2a[, band_names]) se2a_train_mat <- se2a_mat[train_idx, ] se2a_test_mat  <- se2a_mat[test_idx, ]  train_df <- cbind(LUT_train, se2a[train_idx, band_names]) test_df  <- cbind(LUT_test,  se2a[test_idx,  band_names])  r2_f   <- function(obs, pred) 1 - sum((obs - pred)^2) / sum((obs - mean(obs))^2) rmse_f <- function(obs, pred) sqrt(mean((obs - pred)^2))  cat("Train:", length(train_idx), "spectra. Test (held out):", length(test_idx), "spectra.\n") #> Train: 105 spectra. Test (held out): 45 spectra.

title: Trait inversion: merit-function matching, ML, and deep learning
text: method picks “closeness” two spectra measured. nOpt controls many closest training spectra get averaged together final trait estimate (nOpt = 5 – compromise single nearest neighbour, noisy, averaging many, smooths real trait variation): call returns 2-element list: [[1]] (rfl.b) matched reflectance , [[2]] (LUT.best) corresponding trait table – including merit-function’s error value (merit-RMSE, merit-FGE, …) Cab estimate ’re evaluating : merit-RMSE/merit-FGE compare raw band reflectance; merit-DWT compares spectrum’s discrete wavelet transform coefficients instead (sensitive overall shape spectrum rather band’s exact value – can robust band--band noise). merit-NRMSE, merit-MAE, merit-NMB merit-1stD (first-derivative matching, sensitive absorption-feature position/shape absolute reflectance) remaining built-options; custom_stat accepts function(sim, obs) returning single error value place .
code: opt_rmse <- get.inversionOpt(rfl.sensor = se2a_test_mat, rfl.rtm = se2a_train_mat,                               LUT = LUT_train, wave = wl_bands, method = "merit-RMSE", nOpt = 5) opt_fge  <- get.inversionOpt(rfl.sensor = se2a_test_mat, rfl.rtm = se2a_train_mat,                               LUT = LUT_train, wave = wl_bands, method = "merit-FGE", nOpt = 5) opt_dwt  <- get.inversionOpt(rfl.sensor = se2a_test_mat, rfl.rtm = se2a_train_mat,                               LUT = LUT_train, wave = wl_bands, method = "merit-DWT", nOpt = 5) opt_metrics <- data.frame(   method = c("merit-RMSE", "merit-FGE", "merit-DWT"),   R2   = c(r2_f(LUT_test$Cab, opt_rmse[[2]]$Cab), r2_f(LUT_test$Cab, opt_fge[[2]]$Cab), r2_f(LUT_test$Cab, opt_dwt[[2]]$Cab)),   RMSE = c(rmse_f(LUT_test$Cab, opt_rmse[[2]]$Cab), rmse_f(LUT_test$Cab, opt_fge[[2]]$Cab), rmse_f(LUT_test$Cab, opt_dwt[[2]]$Cab)) ) knitr::kable(opt_metrics, digits = 3) plot(LUT_test$Cab, opt_rmse[[2]]$Cab, pch = 19, col = "#2166AC",      xlab = "Observed Cab", ylab = "Predicted Cab (merit-RMSE, nOpt=5)",      main = "LUT merit-function matching") abline(0, 1, col = "grey40", lty = 2)

title: MARMIT + PROSAIL: realistic soil moisture in canopy simulations

Generate a Lookup Table (LUT) for PROSAIL inputs  inputs.prosail <- ToolsRTM::inputsPROSAIL # Create a LUT with 1 entry using the defined PROSAIL inputs df.LUT <- as.data.frame(ToolsRTM::getLUT(inputs = inputs.prosail, nLUT = 1, setseed = 1234))  # 2. Simulate spectral reflectance using PROSAIL and apply BRDF effect  # Simulate reflectance values using the PROSAIL model for the first LUT entry reflectance_values <- ToolsRTM::foursail(inputLUT = df.LUT[1,], rsoil = rsoil, LeafModel = 'PROSPECT-PRO') rdot <- reflectance_values[[1]]  # Direct reflectance rsot <- reflectance_values[[2]]  # Diffuse reflectance  # Compute the Bidirectional Reflectance Factor (BRF) using BRDF effects reflectance_values <- ToolsRTM::Compute_BRF(rdot = rdot, rsot = rsot,                                             tts = df.LUT[1, 'tts'],                                             data.light = ToolsRTM::dataSpec_PDB) # Convert the reflectance values to a matrix for further processing sim.matrix <- as.matrix(t(reflectance_values)) colnames(sim.matrix)=paste0("X",wavelength) # 3. Convolve the simulated reflectance with a sensor-specific SRF and plot the result  # Here, we use the Sentinel-2A sensor for spectral resampling and plotting convolved_spectra <- get.spectra.convolved(rfl = sim.matrix, sensor = "Sentinel2a", plot.spectra = TRUE) } # }

text: simulation.type character. "optical" (ToolsRTM , canopy reflectance) "scope" (SCOPEinR, full energy balance). "scope": SCOPEinR's naming, e.g. "fluspect-CX". canopy.model character. Canopy model name. "optical": "fourSAIL", "foursail2", "INFORM" (three real canopy models ToolsRTM). "scope": SCOPEinR's naming, e.g. "fourSAIL". optipar optical parameters. "optical", passed Fluspect variants used. "scope", passed SCOPEinR (e.g. SCOPEinR::optipar2021.Pro.CX). options.SCOPE SCOPE run-options table (used simulation.type = "scope" – see SCOPEinR's documentation structure). parallel logical. "scope" : run parallel via SCOPEinR::get.SCOPE.parallel() instead SCOPEinR::get.SCOPE(). Default FALSE. get.outputs character. "scope" : SCOPE outputs return, e.g. "". Default "". get.plots logical. "scope" : whether SCOPEinR generate diagnostic plots. Default FALSE. ... additional arguments passed underlying simulate_RTM() / SCOPEinR call.

title: Run a vegetation reflectance/energy-balance simulation, choosing models interactively — run_simulation
text: "optical": output simulate_RTM() (reflectance components). "scope": output SCOPEinR's get.SCOPE()/get.SCOPE.parallel() (reflectance, fluorescence, radiance, energy-balance fluxes).

title: Run a vegetation reflectance/energy-balance simulation, choosing models interactively — run_simulation
text: "optical" – canopy reflectance , atmosphere/energy balance. Runs entirely within ToolsRTM via simulate_RTM(). Fast, good building large LUTs inversion. "scope" – full Soil-Canopy-Observation-Photochemistry-Energy balance simulation (reflectance + fluorescence + radiance + energy fluxes), via SCOPEinR. Requires SCOPEinR package installed – function checks explicitly gives informative error (real GitLab install command) rather cryptic "find function" missing, since SCOPEinR companion package, hard dependency ToolsRTM. function invent simulation logic : "optical" path calls existing, tested simulate_RTM(); "scope" path calls SCOPEinR's get.SCOPE() / get.SCOPE.parallel() using argument names confirmed real teaching scripts using packages together.

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Optical-only simulation (ToolsRTM alone, fast, no energy balance) inputs <- ToolsRTM::inputsPROSAIL LUT <- as.data.frame(ToolsRTM::getLUT(inputs = inputs, nLUT = 1, setseed = 1234)) sim <- run_simulation(   simulation.type = "optical",   inputLUT = LUT[1, ], rsoil = rsoil,   leaf.model = "PROSPECT-PRO", canopy.model = "fourSAIL" )  # Full SCOPE simulation with energy balance (needs SCOPEinR installed) scope_opts <- read.table("Tables/inputs/setoptions.csv", header = TRUE, sep = ",") sim_scope <- run_simulation(   simulation.type = "scope",   inputLUT = LUT, options.SCOPE = scope_opts,   optipar = SCOPEinR::optipar2021.Pro.CX,   leaf.model = "fluspect-CX", canopy.model = "fourSAIL",   parallel = TRUE, get.outputs = "ALL" ) } # }
